advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reference `git_fetch._GIT_TIMEOUT` at call time in repo_snapshot._ensure_blobs_present (or expose a helper) so both fetch paths share a single source of truth for the timeout.
evidence: src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:69 imports `_GIT_TIMEOUT` into the module namespace (bound by value at import)
No test exercises _ensure_blobs_present's timeout, so the divergence is latent rather than currently failing.
advisory.finding: repo_snapshot.py imports `_GIT_TIMEOUT` by value (`from rebar._snapshot.git_fetch import _GIT_TIMEOUT`) and uses it in _ensure_blobs_present's subprocess.run timeout, but fetch_origin/git_run read the module-global git_fetch._GIT_TIMEOUT. Monkeypatching git_fetch._GIT_TIMEOUT (as the tight_stall fixture does) will NOT affect the _ensure_blobs_present timeout in repo_snapshot, so the two paths' effective timeouts can silently diverge under a patched/retuned value.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the multiplied worst-case fetch latency (two fetch_origin calls x _STALL_ATTEMPTS x _GIT_TIMEOUT) is an acceptable bound versus the prior single 300s ceiling.
evidence: resolve_ref calls fetch_origin twice: src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:234 and :240-242
Note the TimeoutExpired branch raises immediately (no retry), so this only bites a stall-marker path across the two fetch_origin calls.
dropped.finding: resolve_ref can now invoke fetch_origin twice (general + targeted), each with up to _STALL_ATTEMPTS (default 3) retries at _GIT_TIMEOUT (300s) each. For a failure that is NOT a stall the retry does not trigger, but for a stall each attempt's wall-clock backstop is still 300s, so a pathological remote that hangs *without* emitting the low-speed marker (e.g. a wedged credential helper that trips TimeoutExpired) is bounded per-attempt but the general+targeted pair still multiplies worst-case exposure. Worth confirming the multiplied worst-case (up to 2*3*300s) is acceptable versus the single 300s ceiling it replaced.
